newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Canberra replaces bonds with tax rebates - paper.
newsitem.headline: Canberra replaces bonds with tax rebates - paper.

text.p: The Australian government will announce in its 1997/98 budget a A$75 million a year tax rebate scheme for rail and road projects to replace the halted infrastructure bonds system, a newspaper reported on Thursday.
Cabinet had decided not to offer concessions for investment in power and water projects and to administer the scheme through the tax office, The Australian Financial Review said.
The new concessions would be capped at A$75 million a year, with about A$37 million in the first year, it said in the unsourced report.
